test_focus: telemetry exporter — bundle per-agent telemetry from multiple agents into a single JSON file for cross-deployment analysis. Optional privacy mode strips metadata. The infrastructure unlocks future studies of real-user dreamscape behavior across deployments.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

module_changes: bog_agents_cli/commands/general.py — registered the export subcommand for autocomplete + help text
public_api: list_agents_with_telemetry() -> list[str]  # discover all agents with a telemetry log
export_telemetry_bundle(output_path, agent_ids=None, since=None, include_metadata=True) -> dict[str, Any]

bundle_schema.include_metadata: bool — when False, events are bare {ts, kind, agent_id}

implementation.privacy_mode: include_metadata=False strips dream titles, injection styles, content categories — keeps only event counts + timestamps. Useful for cross-org aggregation where individual prompt content shouldn't leak.
tests_cover: list_agents_with_telemetry returns only agents with actual logs (not just profile files)
export bundle includes all agents + sums correctly
privacy mode strips metadata (no prompt-derived content leaks)

live_demo.reasoning: Phase 25 already demonstrated the upstream telemetry pipeline end-to-end. Phase 28 is just the bundler — exercised by 5 unit tests against synthetic events. A real live demo would require accumulating events from real usage, which is exactly what the exporter enables for future research.

what_this_unlocks: Operators can run `/dreamscape export ~/telemetry.json` to pack their dreamscape activity into a single portable file.
Privacy-conscious users can use `/dreamscape export --no-metadata` for aggregated counts without dream titles or content categories — share counts without sharing content.

Future Phase 29+ analyses can pool telemetry across deployments. The campaign's offline measurements (Phases 10-26) are sturdy proxies; the exporter unlocks the real-world signal we've been waiting to measure.
An operator who runs dreamscape across 5 different projects can `/dreamscape export` and see aggregate dream count, helped rate, cost — across all of them — without manually grepping JSONL files.

feature_verdicts.list_agents_with_telemetry: sings — only returns agents with actual log files, ignores profile-only dirs
feature_verdicts.export_telemetry_bundle: sings — schema-versioned bundle, agent-by-agent summary + raw events
feature_verdicts.privacy_mode: sings — strips metadata cleanly while preserving aggregate counts
feature_verdicts.auto_discovery: sings — agent_ids=None auto-enumerates the agents dir

known_limitations: The bundle is JSON, not JSONL — for very large logs (>10MB) streaming serialization would be preferable. Acceptable at current scales.
No remote-export adapter (S3, HTTPS POST, etc.) — operators must manually move the bundle. Easy to add as a future extension; intentionally not shipped yet so security review can land first.

The privacy mode strips event metadata but keeps per-agent agg summaries which include `dreams_by_category` and `injections_by_style`. These are very coarse aggregations (no individual prompts leak) but a 'maximum privacy' mode could blank these too.
No schema-version forward-compatibility logic — schema_version=1 is recorded but readers must handle future versions themselves.
verdict: READY TO MERGE — clean infrastructure ship. Unlocks future cross-deployment analysis without changing modal behavior.
next_steps: Phase 29 (suggested): once Phase 25 telemetry accumulates from real usage, run /dreamscape export and compare to the offline judge proxies from the campaign. Disagreement is itself informative.
Phase 32 (suggested): pluggable remote-export adapters (HTTPS POST + auth). For deployments that want to forward telemetry to a central observability backend.

Phase 33 (suggested): maximum-privacy export mode — strip even the per-agent summary categories/styles, leaving only timestamp + kind + agent_id. For environments with strict data-residency requirements.
